newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA URGED TO SPEED UP REMOVAL OF FX CONTROLS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA URGED TO SPEED UP REMOVAL OF FX CONTROLS.

text.p: South Africa should quickly consolidate gains made from recent economic reforms and abolish exchange controls as quickly as possible, Board of Executors economic adviser Rob Lee said on Wednesday.
In his latest Investment Outlook, Lee said that there had been an impressive acceleration in policy reform and a leap in economic policy credibility in recent months.

"The last few months have seen increasing evidence that the government has taken to heart the message from financial markets that economic reforms need to be implemented with much greater urgency," Lee said.

These reforms included continued tariff cuts, progress in the privatisation drive, the Reserve Bank's withdrawal from the forward cover market, improved tax collection, the cancellation of 3.1 billion rand in roll over funds and a tough line on spendng limits for 1997/98.
"Now that expectations have been raised it is all the more critical that the next few months sees the full implementation of the (reform) programme.

"If so, we can look forward to falling inflation and interest rates, foreign capital inflows financing a sustainable level of current account deficits and accelerating economic growth from 1998 onwards."
There were several options open to government in further dismantling exchange controls.
Lee said it could broaden the asset swap system to include corporate swaps while making the administration of controls more streamlined and flexible.
It could also allow institutions to invest more cash flows into foreign assets and give individual residents access to dollar accounts.

Lee said new government bonds could also be issued to emigrants, a move recently mooted by Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals, who would be able to use blocked rands to buy stock with the capital remittable on maturity.
"We would encourage the authorities to move as fast as possible now, when circumstances have again become favourable," he said.

Lee warned that the renewed inflow of foreign capital and large injections of funds through Telkom's privatisation could threaten the Reserve Banks' control of short term interest rates and result in the rand strengthening too much.

"A major relaxation of capital controls would fulfil the fourfold objectives of controlling domestic liquidity, preventing unsustainable currency strength, raising the long-term growth potential of the economy and reducing its future risk profile to investors," Lee said.
